composite_tax_morale_score.description: Composite tax morale score (0-1) from Afrobarometer R8 Tanzania. Weighted: civic duty 30%, trust 35%, non-avoidance 20%, reciprocity 15%.

policy_implications.key_finding: 71% of Tanzanians agree citizens should pay taxes (civic duty) but only 43% say government listens to them. This 28pp gap is the reciprocity deficit — citizens are willing to comply if government responds. The behavioral lifecycle strategy directly addresses this gap.
policy_implications.tax_morale_baseline: Composite tax morale score of 59.8% from Afrobarometer. This calibrates the tax morale model in economic_model.py — baseline was assumed at 30.6%, Afrobarometer evidence suggests it is higher at ~59.8% but suppressed by reciprocity deficit.
policy_implications.corruption_perception: 42% believe most/all officials are corrupt. This directly reduces voluntary compliance. Visible tax returns campaign (intervention) is designed to counter this specifically.
